title: REVEALING POTENTIAL BIASES IN LLM-BASED RECOMMENDER SYSTEMS IN THE COLD START SETTING

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual prompting using gender-related attributes (e.g., 'boy', 'girl', 'male', 'female') to analyze the shift in recommended item genres, specifically measuring the proportion of action movies in the top-20 recommendations.

Evaluating the proportion of Western-produced content recommended across different user personas (e.g., various nationalities, continents) compared to a neutral baseline to expose default cultural alignment.
Measuring the divergence (using IOU similarity) of recommendation lists generated for users with different racial attributes (Black, Asian, Hispanic, White) compared to a neutral user baseline.
Measuring recommendation list divergence and the ratio of Western content recommended when prompting the model with different religious identities (Buddhist, Christian, Muslim).
Computing the divergence of top-k recommendation lists generated for users conditioned on different parental occupation attributes (Student, Teacher, Doctor, Worker, Writer).
Prompting the model with different country attributes (e.g., British, Brazilian, Chinese, American) and computing the similarity of the generated recommendation lists against a neutral baseline.
